for name, plugin_subcommand in plugin_subcommands.items():
        # bundled previews may intentionally override a built-in command by
        # extending its parser rather than replacing it
        is_preview_builtin = (
            name in BUILTIN_COMMANDS
            and is_preview_subcommand(plugin_subcommand)
            and name in BUILTIN_COMMAND_PARSERS
        )

        # if the name of the plugin-based subcommand overlaps a built-in
        # subcommand (and isn't a bundled preview), we print an error
        if name in BUILTIN_COMMANDS and not is_preview_builtin:
            log.error(
                dals(
                    f"""
                    The plugin '{name}' is trying to override the built-in command
                    with the same name, which is not allowed.

                    Please uninstall the plugin to stop seeing this error message.
                    """
                )
            )
            continue

        if is_preview_builtin:
            # start from the built-in parser, then let the preview extend it
            parser = BUILTIN_COMMAND_PARSERS[name](sub_parsers)
        else:
            parser = sub_parsers.add_parser(
                name,
                description=plugin_subcommand.summary,
                help=plugin_subcommand.summary,
                add_help=False,  # defer to subcommand's help processing
            )

        # case 1: plugin extends the parser
        if plugin_subcommand.configure_parser:
            plugin_subcommand.configure_parser(parser)

            # attempt to add standard help processing, will fail if plugin defines
            # their own; built-in parsers already handle help themselves
            if not is_preview_builtin:
                try:
                    add_parser_help(parser)
                except argparse.ArgumentError:
                    pass

        # case 2: plugin has their own parser, see _GreedySubParsersAction
        elif not is_preview_builtin:
            parser.greedy = True

        # underscore prefixed indicating this is not a normal argparse argument
        parser.set_defaults(_plugin_subcommand=plugin_subcommand)
